JOB.1.1-3.text: Job lived in Uz and feared God

JOB.1.4-5.text: Job offers sacrifices for his children after feasts

JOB.1.6-8.text: The LORD points Satan to Job as blameless

JOB.1.9-12.text: The LORD lets Satan test Job’s possessions

JOB.1.18-19.text: A wind collapses the house and Job’s children die

JOB.1.20-22.text: Job mourns and still worships God

JOB.2.1-2.text: Satan again comes before the LORD

JOB.2.3-3.text: The LORD says Job still keeps his integrity

JOB.2.4-6.text: The LORD lets Satan strike Job but not kill him

JOB.2.7-8.text: Satan covers Job with painful boils

JOB.2.9-10.text: Job’s wife says to curse God, but Job refuses

JOB.2.11-11.text: Job’s three friends come to comfort him

JOB.2.12-13.text: Job’s friends weep and sit silent with him seven days

JOB.3.1-3.text: Job curses the day he was born

JOB.3.4-5.text: Job wishes his birth day would become darkness

JOB.3.6-7.text: Job wants that night removed from the year

JOB.3.8-10.text: Job curses the night that did not stop his birth

JOB.3.11-12.text: Job asks why he did not die at birth

JOB.3.13-14.text: Job says he would now rest with kings and counselors

JOB.3.15-16.text: Job wishes he had been hidden like a stillborn child

JOB.3.17-19.text: Job says the grave gives rest to all people

JOB.3.20-22.text: Job asks why suffering people must live

JOB.3.23-24.text: Job asks why God gives life to a man in pain

JOB.3.25-26.text: Job says what he feared has happened

JOB.4.1-3.text: Eliphaz reminds Job that Job has helped many people

JOB.4.4-6.text: Eliphaz says Job is now troubled and should trust God

JOB.4.7-9.text: Eliphaz says God destroys those who sow trouble

JOB.4.10-11.text: Eliphaz compares the wicked to lions that perish

JOB.4.12-13.text: Eliphaz says a secret word came to him in the night

JOB.4.14-15.text: Eliphaz trembles when a spirit passes by

JOB.4.16-17.text: Eliphaz hears a voice ask if people are purer than God

JOB.4.18-19.text: Eliphaz says God finds fault even with his angels

JOB.4.20-21.text: Eliphaz says people die without wisdom

JOB.5.1-3.text: Eliphaz says resentment and envy kill fools

JOB.5.4-5.text: Eliphaz says a fool’s sons and harvest are lost

JOB.5.6-7.text: Eliphaz says people are born to trouble

JOB.5.8-10.text: Eliphaz tells Job to appeal to God, who does great things

JOB.5.11-13.text: Eliphaz says God lifts the lowly and stops the crafty

JOB.5.14-16.text: Eliphaz says God saves the needy and gives the poor hope

JOB.5.17-19.text: Eliphaz tells Job that God corrects and also heals

JOB.5.20-22.text: Eliphaz says God will keep Job safe from harm

JOB.5.23-25.text: Eliphaz promises Job peace, safety and many descendants

JOB.5.26-27.text: Eliphaz says Job will live long; Job should listen

JOB.6.1-3.text: Job says his grief is heavier than the sand of the seas

JOB.6.4-6.text: Job says God’s arrows have pierced him

JOB.6.7-9.text: Job wishes that God would crush him and end his life

JOB.6.10-11.text: Job has comfort in God’s words but little strength to hope

JOB.6.12-13.text: Job asks if his strength is like stone

JOB.6.14-17.text: Job says his friends are faithless like dry streams

JOB.6.18-20.text: Job compares his friends to caravans that find no water

JOB.6.21-23.text: Job says his friends have been no help

JOB.6.24-25.text: Job asks his friends to show him his error

JOB.6.26-27.text: Job says his friends treat his cry as wind

JOB.6.28-30.text: Job asks his friends to look at him and be fair

JOB.7.1-3.text: Job says human life is hard work and misery

JOB.7.4-5.text: Job describes his sleepless nights and sick body

JOB.7.6-7.text: Job says his days pass quickly and life is a breath

JOB.7.8-10.text: Job says the dead do not return home

JOB.7.11-12.text: Job will not be silent and asks why God guards him

JOB.7.13-15.text: Job says God frightens him with dreams and visions

JOB.7.16-18.text: Job asks God to leave him alone, for life is a breath

JOB.7.19-20.text: Job asks God why Job has become God’s target

JOB.7.21-21.text: Job asks God to pardon his sin before he dies

JOB.8.1-3.text: Bildad says Job speaks like wind and God is just

JOB.8.4-5.text: Bildad says Job should seek God and ask for mercy

JOB.8.6-7.text: Bildad says God will restore Job if Job is pure

JOB.8.8-10.text: Bildad tells Job to learn from past generations

JOB.8.11-12.text: Bildad says papyrus and reeds die without water

JOB.8.13-15.text: Bildad says the hope of the godless will perish

JOB.8.16-18.text: Bildad compares the godless to a plant pulled up

JOB.8.19-20.text: Bildad says God does not reject the blameless

JOB.8.21-22.text: Bildad says God will give Job joy again

JOB.9.1-3.text: Job asks how a person can be right before God

JOB.9.4-6.text: Job says God is very strong and shakes the earth

JOB.9.7-9.text: Job says God made the stars and rules the sky

JOB.9.10-12.text: Job says no one can stop what God does

JOB.9.13-15.text: Job says he could not answer God, only beg for mercy

JOB.9.16-18.text: Job believes God would not listen and would crush him

JOB.9.19-20.text: Job says his own mouth would declare him guilty

JOB.9.21-24.text: Job says God destroys both the blameless and the wicked

JOB.9.25-26.text: Job says his days pass quickly

JOB.9.27-29.text: Job fears God will not declare him innocent

JOB.9.30-31.text: Job says washing himself clean would not help

JOB.9.32-33.text: Job says no mediator stands between him and God

JOB.9.34-35.text: Job wants God to stop frightening him so he can speak

JOB.10.1-3.text: Job complains to God and asks not to be condemned

JOB.10.4-7.text: Job asks if God sees as a man sees

JOB.10.8-9.text: Job reminds God that God made him from clay

JOB.10.10-11.text: Job says God formed him with skin, flesh, and bones

JOB.10.12-14.text: Job says God gave him life but watches for his sin

JOB.10.15-16.text: Job says he is in shame and God hunts him

JOB.10.17-17.text: Job says God brings new troubles against him

JOB.10.18-19.text: Job asks why God let him be born

JOB.10.20-22.text: Job asks God to leave him alone before he dies

JOB.11.1-3.text: Zophar says Job talks too much and must be rebuked

JOB.11.4-6.text: Zophar says God would show Job his sin

JOB.11.7-9.text: Zophar says no one can fully understand God

JOB.11.10-12.text: Zophar says no one can stop God from judging

JOB.11.13-14.text: Zophar urges Job to turn to God and put away sin

JOB.11.15-17.text: Zophar promises Job a life without shame or fear

JOB.11.18-19.text: Zophar says Job will have hope and live in safety

JOB.11.20-20.text: Zophar says the wicked will lose hope

JOB.12.1-3.text: Job says he is as wise as his friends

JOB.12.4-6.text: Job is laughed at, while wicked people live in safety

JOB.12.7-8.text: Job says animals, birds and fish can teach his friends

JOB.12.9-10.text: Job says God holds the life of every living thing

JOB.12.11-12.text: Job says the old have wisdom and understanding

JOB.12.13-15.text: Job says God has wisdom and power over all things

JOB.12.16-18.text: Job says God humbles counselors, judges and kings

JOB.12.19-21.text: Job says God overthrows priests, elders and nobles

JOB.12.22-23.text: Job says God raises up nations and destroys nations

JOB.12.24-25.text: Job says God makes earth’s leaders wander without light

JOB.13.1-2.text: Job says he knows as much as his friends

JOB.13.3-5.text: Job wants to argue with God and calls friends worthless

JOB.13.6-8.text: Job asks if his friends should lie to defend God

JOB.13.9-10.text: Job warns his friends that God will rebuke partiality

JOB.13.11-12.text: Job says God’s majesty should terrify his friends

JOB.13.13-15.text: Job says he will hope in God even if God kills him

JOB.13.16-17.text: Job says no godless person can come before God

JOB.13.18-19.text: Job has prepared his case and expects to be proved right

JOB.13.20-22.text: Job asks God to stop hurting and frightening him

JOB.13.23-25.text: Job asks God to show his sin and why God opposes him

JOB.13.26-28.text: Job says God watches him closely and records his sins

JOB.14.1-3.text: Job says human life is short and full of trouble

JOB.14.4-6.text: Job asks God to look away and let people rest

JOB.14.7-9.text: Job says a cut tree has hope to grow again

JOB.14.10-12.text: Job says a man dies and does not rise again

JOB.14.13-14.text: Job wishes God would hide him until God’s anger passes

JOB.14.15-17.text: Job imagines God would call him and forgive his sin

JOB.14.18-19.text: Job says God destroys human hope like water on stones

JOB.14.20-22.text: Job says a dead man cannot know what happens to his sons

JOB.15.1-3.text: Eliphaz says Job speaks empty and useless words

JOB.15.4-6.text: Eliphaz says Job’s own words show he is guilty

JOB.15.7-9.text: Eliphaz asks if Job knows more than his friends

JOB.15.10-11.text: Eliphaz says older men agree with him, not Job

JOB.15.12-14.text: Eliphaz asks why Job turns against God

JOB.15.15-16.text: Eliphaz says no human is pure before God

JOB.15.17-18.text: Eliphaz promises to tell what wise men taught

JOB.15.19-21.text: Eliphaz says a wicked man suffers all his days

JOB.15.22-24.text: Eliphaz says the wicked live in fear of death

JOB.15.25-26.text: Eliphaz says the wicked man fights against God

JOB.15.27-28.text: Eliphaz says the rich wicked man will lose his home

JOB.15.29-30.text: Eliphaz says the wicked man’s wealth will not last

JOB.15.31-33.text: Eliphaz warns that trusting emptiness brings loss

JOB.15.34-35.text: Eliphaz says the godless will have nothing but trouble

JOB.16.1-3.text: Job says his friends give no comfort

JOB.16.4-5.text: Job says he would comfort friends who suffered like him

JOB.16.6-8.text: Job says God has worn him out

JOB.16.9-10.text: Job says God and people attack him

JOB.16.11-12.text: Job says God has given him to wicked men

JOB.16.13-14.text: Job says God attacks him without mercy

JOB.16.15-17.text: Job mourns, yet says his hands are free of violence

JOB.16.18-19.text: Job says his witness in heaven will speak for him

JOB.16.20-22.text: Job weeps to God and expects to die soon

JOB.17.1-3.text: Job says his spirit is broken and the grave awaits

JOB.17.4-5.text: Job says God has closed his friends’ minds

JOB.17.6-8.text: Job says people mock him and his body is weak

JOB.17.9-10.text: Job says the righteous stay strong; friends are not wise

JOB.17.11-12.text: Job says his days are gone and his plans are broken

JOB.17.13-16.text: Job asks where his hope is as he faces the grave

JOB.18.1-2.text: Bildad tells Job to stop talking and show sense

JOB.18.3-4.text: Bildad asks why Job treats his friends as stupid

JOB.18.5-6.text: Bildad says the wicked man’s light goes out

JOB.18.7-8.text: Bildad says the wicked man walks into a net

JOB.18.9-11.text: Bildad says traps and terrors catch the wicked man

JOB.18.12-13.text: Bildad says the wicked man loses strength and health

JOB.18.14-15.text: Bildad says the wicked man is taken to death

JOB.18.16-17.text: Bildad says the wicked man is forgotten on earth

JOB.18.18-20.text: Bildad says the wicked man is driven out and forgotten

JOB.18.21-21.text: Bildad says this is the fate of those who do not know God

JOB.19.1-2.text: Job asks his friends how long they will hurt him with words

JOB.19.3-4.text: Job says his friends have shamelessly insulted him many times

JOB.19.5-6.text: Job says God has wronged him and trapped him

JOB.19.7-9.text: Job says God gives no justice and has taken his honor

JOB.19.10-12.text: Job says God attacks him like an enemy

JOB.19.13-14.text: Job says his relatives and friends have abandoned him

JOB.19.15-16.text: Job says even his guests and servants treat him as a stranger

JOB.19.17-19.text: Job says his wife, family and close friends turn from him

JOB.19.20-22.text: Job asks his friends to pity him and stop attacking him

JOB.19.23-24.text: Job wishes his words could be written down forever

JOB.19.25-27.text: Job says he knows his Redeemer lives and he will see God

JOB.19.28-29.text: Job warns his friends that they will face God’s judgment

JOB.20.1-3.text: Zophar says he must answer Job because he feels insulted

JOB.20.4-5.text: Zophar says the joy of the wicked lasts only a short time

JOB.20.6-7.text: Zophar says the proud wicked man will perish and be gone

JOB.20.8-9.text: Zophar says the wicked man will vanish like a dream

JOB.20.10-11.text: Zophar says the wicked man’s sons will pay back the poor

JOB.20.12-14.text: Zophar says evil tastes sweet to the wicked but turns to poison

JOB.20.15-16.text: Zophar says God will make the wicked man give up his wealth

JOB.20.17-19.text: Zophar says the wicked man loses wealth gained by oppressing the poor

JOB.20.20-22.text: Zophar says the greedy wicked man will fall into misery

JOB.20.23-25.text: Zophar says God will pour out anger on the wicked man

JOB.20.26-27.text: Zophar says fire, heaven and earth will turn against the wicked

JOB.20.28-29.text: Zophar says God’s wrath takes the wicked man’s house and goods

JOB.21.1-3.text: Job asks his friends to listen to him before they mock

JOB.21.4-6.text: Job says his complaint is serious and his friends should be shocked

JOB.21.7-9.text: Job asks why the wicked live long, safe and strong

JOB.21.10-12.text: Job says the wicked have rich flocks and happy children

JOB.21.13-15.text: Job says the wicked live in peace but reject God

JOB.21.16-18.text: Job asks how often the wicked really suffer disaster

JOB.21.19-21.text: Job says the wicked man himself should be punished by God

JOB.21.22-24.text: Job says one man dies healthy and secure

JOB.21.25-26.text: Job says another man dies bitter, and both lie in dust

JOB.21.27-28.text: Job says his friends plan to wrong him

JOB.21.29-30.text: Job says the evil man escapes the day of calamity

JOB.21.31-33.text: Job says an evil man is honored at his burial

JOB.21.34-34.text: Job says his friends’ comfort is empty and false

JOB.22.1-3.text: Eliphaz asks if Job’s goodness helps God

JOB.22.4-5.text: Eliphaz says Job’s wickedness is great

JOB.22.6-8.text: Eliphaz accuses Job of harming the poor and hungry

JOB.22.9-11.text: Eliphaz says Job harmed widows and now faces danger

JOB.22.12-14.text: Eliphaz says Job thinks God cannot see or judge

JOB.22.15-17.text: Eliphaz asks if Job will follow wicked men’s old path

JOB.22.18-20.text: Eliphaz says the righteous are glad when the wicked fall

JOB.22.21-22.text: Eliphaz urges Job to make peace with God

JOB.22.23-25.text: Eliphaz says Job will be restored if he returns to God

JOB.22.26-28.text: Eliphaz promises Job joy in God and answered prayer

JOB.22.29-30.text: Eliphaz says God will rescue others through Job

JOB.23.1-2.text: Job says his complaint is bitter and God’s hand is heavy

JOB.23.3-5.text: Job wishes he could find God and plead his case

JOB.23.6-7.text: Job believes God would listen to an upright man

JOB.23.8-9.text: Job cannot find God in any direction

JOB.23.10-12.text: Job says God knows his way and he has obeyed God

JOB.23.13-14.text: Job says no one can oppose God’s plans

JOB.23.15-17.text: Job is terrified of God but not silenced by darkness

JOB.24.1-1.text: Job asks why God does not set times for judgment

JOB.24.2-4.text: Job says wicked men steal from the poor and fatherless

JOB.24.5-7.text: Job says the poor search for food and have no clothing

JOB.24.8-10.text: Job says the poor are cold and hungry

JOB.24.11-12.text: Job says workers suffer, yet God charges no one

JOB.24.13-14.text: Job says the murderer kills the poor at night

JOB.24.15-17.text: Job says adulterers and thieves hide in the dark

JOB.24.18-19.text: Job says sinners are like foam and go to Sheol

JOB.24.20-21.text: Job says the wicked are forgotten and harm widows

JOB.24.22-23.text: God drags away the mighty and watches the wicked

JOB.24.24-25.text: Job says the wicked are exalted briefly, then gone

JOB.25.1-3.text: Bildad says God rules and his light shines on all

JOB.25.4-6.text: Bildad asks how a man can be pure before God

JOB.26.1-4.text: Job asks Bildad whose spirit spoke through him

JOB.26.5-6.text: Job says the dead and Sheol are open before God

JOB.26.7-8.text: God hangs the earth on nothing and wraps water in clouds

JOB.26.9-10.text: God covers the moon and marks the horizon on the waters

JOB.26.11-12.text: God shakes heaven and defeats Rahab by his power

JOB.26.13-14.text: Job says people hear only a faint whisper of God’s power

JOB.27.1-3.text: Job swears by the living God while he still has breath

JOB.27.4-5.text: Job refuses to lie or to say his friends are right

JOB.27.6-6.text: Job holds to his righteousness and has a clear conscience

JOB.27.7-7.text: Job wishes his enemy to be like the wicked

JOB.27.8-10.text: The godless man has no hope when God ends his life

JOB.27.11-12.text: Job will teach his friends about God’s power

JOB.27.13-14.text: The wicked man’s children will die by the sword or hunger

JOB.27.15-17.text: The wicked man’s riches will go to the righteous

JOB.27.18-19.text: The wicked man’s house is weak and his wealth soon gone

JOB.27.20-21.text: Terrors and a storm sweep the wicked man away

JOB.27.22-23.text: The storm mocks the wicked man and drives him away

JOB.28.1-2.text: People mine silver, gold, iron and copper from the earth

JOB.28.3-4.text: Miners search deep dark places far from people

JOB.28.5-6.text: Miners find sapphires and gold in the earth’s rocks

JOB.28.7-8.text: No bird or animal knows the path to the mine

JOB.28.9-11.text: Miners overturn mountains to find hidden treasure

JOB.28.12-14.text: Job asks where wisdom is found; the sea does not have it

JOB.28.15-17.text: Wisdom cannot be bought with gold, silver or jewels

JOB.28.18-19.text: Wisdom is worth more than coral, rubies or topaz

JOB.28.20-22.text: Wisdom is hidden from all living things

JOB.28.23-25.text: God knows where wisdom is, for he sees all the earth

JOB.28.26-28.text: God tells people that fear of the Lord is wisdom

JOB.29.1-3.text: Job longs for the days when God watched over him

JOB.29.4-6.text: Job remembers when God’s friendship blessed his home

JOB.29.7-8.text: Young and old men honored Job at the city gate

JOB.29.9-10.text: Princes and nobles became silent before Job

JOB.29.11-13.text: Job helped the poor, the fatherless and widows

JOB.29.14-16.text: Job did right and helped the blind, lame and needy

JOB.29.17-19.text: Job stopped the unjust and hoped for a long, safe life

JOB.29.20-22.text: Men listened to Job and waited for his advice

JOB.29.23-24.text: People waited for Job’s words as for rain

JOB.29.25-25.text: Job led the people like a king and comforted mourners

JOB.30.1-3.text: Young men whose fathers were poor now mock Job

JOB.30.4-6.text: Outcast men ate roots and lived in holes in the ground

JOB.30.7-8.text: Job says the outcasts were driven from the land

JOB.30.9-11.text: Job says the outcasts now mock and spit at him

JOB.30.12-13.text: A crowd of outcasts attacks Job and ruins his way

JOB.30.14-14.text: The attackers rush in like water through a broken wall

JOB.30.15-15.text: Terrors take away Job’s dignity and prosperity

JOB.30.16-17.text: Job is in constant pain day and night

JOB.30.18-19.text: Job says God throws him into the mud

JOB.30.20-21.text: Job cries to God, but God does not answer

JOB.30.22-23.text: Job says God tosses him in a storm toward death

JOB.30.24-26.text: Job wept for others, yet evil came when he hoped for good

JOB.30.27-29.text: Job is restless, darkened, and alone in his suffering

JOB.30.30-31.text: Job’s skin is black and his songs are of mourning

JOB.31.1-2.text: Job says he made a promise not to look with desire

JOB.31.3-4.text: Job says God sees his steps and judges the unjust

JOB.31.5-6.text: Job asks God to weigh him fairly if he lied

JOB.31.7-8.text: Job accepts loss of his crops if he has sinned

JOB.31.9-10.text: Job rejects adultery and accepts punishment if guilty

JOB.31.11-12.text: Job says adultery is a crime that destroys harvests

JOB.31.13-15.text: Job treats his servants fairly because God made all

JOB.31.16-18.text: Job says he fed the poor, widows and the fatherless

JOB.31.19-21.text: Job says he clothed the needy and did not harm the fatherless

JOB.31.22-23.text: Job says his arm should fall if guilty, for he fears God

JOB.31.24-25.text: Job says he never trusted in gold or wealth

JOB.31.26-28.text: Job says he never worshiped the sun or moon

JOB.31.29-30.text: Job says he never rejoiced when an enemy suffered

JOB.31.31-32.text: Job says his house welcomed strangers and travelers

JOB.31.33-34.text: Job says he did not hide his sins out of fear

JOB.31.35-37.text: Job wants God to answer him and accuse him openly

JOB.31.38-40.text: Job says he never wronged his land or its workers

JOB.32.1-2.text: Elihu becomes angry with Job for justifying himself

JOB.32.3-5.text: Elihu is angry because the friends could not answer Job

JOB.32.6-7.text: Elihu says he was afraid to speak because he is young

JOB.32.8-10.text: Elihu says understanding comes from God, not only age

JOB.32.11-12.text: Elihu says none of the friends proved Job wrong

JOB.32.13-14.text: Elihu will not answer Job with the friends’ arguments

JOB.32.15-16.text: Elihu says the friends have no more to say

JOB.32.17-19.text: Elihu says he is full of words and must speak

JOB.32.20-22.text: Elihu says he must speak and will not flatter anyone

JOB.33.1-3.text: Elihu asks Job to listen to his sincere words

JOB.33.4-5.text: Elihu says God made him and invites Job to answer

JOB.33.6-7.text: Elihu says he is, like Job, formed from clay

JOB.33.8-9.text: Elihu repeats Job’s claim that he is pure

JOB.33.10-12.text: Elihu says Job is wrong because God is greater than man

JOB.33.13-15.text: Elihu says God speaks to people in dreams and visions

JOB.33.16-18.text: Elihu says God warns people to turn from wrongdoing

JOB.33.19-20.text: Elihu says pain on a sickbed can also warn a person

JOB.33.21-22.text: Elihu describes a sick man near death

JOB.33.23-24.text: Elihu says a messenger can win mercy for a sick man

JOB.33.25-26.text: Elihu says the man is restored and sees God with joy

JOB.33.27-28.text: Elihu says the saved man admits his sin and sings

JOB.33.29-30.text: Elihu says God does these things to save a man’s life

JOB.33.31-33.text: Elihu tells Job to answer or to listen and learn

JOB.34.1-3.text: Elihu calls the wise men to hear his words

JOB.34.4-6.text: Elihu quotes Job’s claim that God denies him justice

JOB.34.7-9.text: Elihu accuses Job of keeping company with the wicked

JOB.34.10-12.text: Elihu says God never does wrong or twists justice

JOB.34.13-15.text: Elihu says all life depends on God’s breath

JOB.34.16-17.text: Elihu asks Job if he will condemn the just God

JOB.34.18-20.text: Elihu says God favors neither rich nor poor

JOB.34.21-23.text: Elihu says God sees every step and no one can hide

JOB.34.24-25.text: Elihu says God overthrows the mighty in the night

JOB.34.26-28.text: Elihu says God punishes wicked rulers who harm the poor

JOB.34.29-30.text: Elihu says no one can condemn God when he is silent

JOB.34.31-33.text: Elihu says God will not repay Job on Job’s terms

JOB.34.34-35.text: Elihu says wise men will say Job speaks without knowledge

JOB.34.36-37.text: Elihu says Job adds rebellion to his sin

JOB.35.1-3.text: Elihu says Job claims to be more righteous than God

JOB.35.4-5.text: Elihu tells Job to look at the heavens and clouds

JOB.35.6-8.text: Elihu says Job’s sin and goodness do not change God

JOB.35.9-11.text: Elihu says people cry out but do not ask for God

JOB.35.12-14.text: Elihu says God does not answer proud, empty pleas

JOB.35.15-16.text: Elihu says Job speaks many words without knowledge

JOB.36.1-3.text: Elihu says he has more to say for God

JOB.36.4-5.text: Elihu says God is mighty and despises no one

JOB.36.6-7.text: Elihu says God helps the afflicted, not the wicked

JOB.36.8-9.text: Elihu says God warns people who are bound in chains

JOB.36.10-12.text: Elihu says those who obey God prosper, others perish

JOB.36.13-14.text: Elihu says godless people do not cry to God for help

JOB.36.15-16.text: Elihu says God rescues the afflicted and once helped Job

JOB.36.17-18.text: Elihu warns Job not to be led astray by riches

JOB.36.19-21.text: Elihu warns Job not to choose wrong over affliction

JOB.36.22-24.text: Elihu says God is a great teacher and does no wrong

JOB.36.25-26.text: Elihu says God is great beyond human knowledge

JOB.36.27-29.text: Elihu says God sends rain and thunder from the clouds

JOB.36.30-31.text: Elihu says God uses lightning to judge and give food

JOB.36.32-33.text: Elihu says God commands the lightning to hit its mark

JOB.37.1-3.text: Elihu trembles at the thunder of God’s voice

JOB.37.4-6.text: Elihu says God thunders and commands snow and rain

JOB.37.7-9.text: Elihu says God stops people’s work and sends storms

JOB.37.10-11.text: Elihu says God makes ice and fills the clouds

JOB.37.12-13.text: Elihu says God uses clouds to punish or to help

JOB.37.14-15.text: Elihu tells Job to stop and think about God’s wonders

JOB.37.16-17.text: Elihu asks Job about the clouds and God’s knowledge

JOB.37.18-20.text: Elihu says no one can argue a case against God

JOB.37.21-22.text: Elihu says no one can look at God’s golden glory

JOB.37.23-24.text: Elihu says God is powerful and just, so people fear God

JOB.38.1-3.text: The LORD speaks to Job out of the whirlwind

JOB.38.4-5.text: The LORD asks Job who measured the earth

JOB.38.6-7.text: The LORD asks Job who laid the earth’s cornerstone

JOB.38.8-9.text: The LORD asks Job who shut the sea behind doors

JOB.38.10-11.text: The LORD set limits that the sea’s waves cannot pass

JOB.38.12-13.text: The LORD asks Job if Job ever commanded the dawn

JOB.38.14-15.text: Dawn shapes the earth, but light is kept from the wicked

JOB.38.16-18.text: The LORD asks Job if Job has seen the gates of death

JOB.38.19-21.text: The LORD asks Job about the homes of light and darkness

JOB.38.22-24.text: The LORD asks Job about snow, hail and lightning

JOB.38.25-27.text: The LORD asks Job who sends rain to the empty desert

JOB.38.28-30.text: The LORD asks Job who gives birth to rain, ice and frost

JOB.38.31-33.text: The LORD asks Job about the stars and the heavens’ laws

JOB.38.34-35.text: The LORD asks Job if Job can command clouds and lightning

JOB.38.36-38.text: The LORD asks Job who gives wisdom and controls the clouds

JOB.38.39-40.text: The LORD asks Job if Job can feed the lions

JOB.38.41-41.text: The LORD asks Job who feeds the young ravens

JOB.39.1-2.text: The LORD asks Job if Job knows when wild goats give birth

JOB.39.3-4.text: The young of wild goats and deer grow up and leave

JOB.39.5-6.text: The LORD made the wilderness the wild donkey’s home

JOB.39.7-8.text: The wild donkey avoids the city and searches the mountains

JOB.39.9-10.text: The LORD asks Job if the wild ox will work for Job

JOB.39.11-12.text: The LORD asks Job if Job can trust the wild ox’s strength

JOB.39.13-15.text: The ostrich leaves her eggs on the ground

JOB.39.16-18.text: God gave the ostrich no wisdom, yet she laughs at horses

JOB.39.19-20.text: The LORD asks Job if he gave the horse its strength

JOB.39.21-23.text: The war horse is strong and unafraid in battle

JOB.39.24-25.text: The horse is eager when the horn sounds for war

JOB.39.26-26.text: The LORD asks Job if he teaches the hawk to fly

JOB.39.27-28.text: The LORD asks if Job commands the eagle to nest high

JOB.39.29-30.text: The eagle sees food from far away and feeds its young

JOB.40.1-2.text: The LORD asks if Job will argue with God

JOB.40.3-5.text: Job says he is unworthy and will not answer

JOB.40.6-7.text: The LORD tells Job to get ready to answer questions

JOB.40.8-9.text: The LORD asks if Job would condemn God to be right

JOB.40.10-11.text: The LORD tells Job to bring down the proud

JOB.40.12-14.text: The LORD says Job must defeat the wicked to save himself

JOB.40.15-16.text: The LORD shows Job Behemoth, a strong animal

JOB.40.17-18.text: Behemoth has a tail like a cedar and bones like bronze

JOB.40.19-21.text: Behemoth is the greatest of God’s works and lives safely

JOB.40.22-24.text: Behemoth is not afraid; no one can capture him

JOB.41.1-3.text: The LORD asks if Job can catch and control Leviathan

JOB.41.4-6.text: Leviathan will not serve Job or become his pet

JOB.41.7-9.text: No one can fight Leviathan and win

JOB.41.10-12.text: No one can stand against Leviathan, or against God

JOB.41.13-15.text: No one can approach Leviathan’s jaws and scales

JOB.41.16-18.text: Leviathan’s scales are tightly joined, and his eyes shine

JOB.41.19-21.text: Fire and smoke come from Leviathan’s mouth and nose

JOB.41.22-24.text: Leviathan has a strong neck and a chest hard as rock

JOB.41.25-27.text: Strong men fear Leviathan, and weapons cannot hurt him

JOB.41.28-30.text: Arrows, stones and clubs do not harm Leviathan

JOB.41.31-32.text: Leviathan stirs the sea and leaves a shining wake

JOB.41.33-34.text: Leviathan has no equal and is king over the proud

JOB.42.1-3.text: Job tells the LORD he spoke without understanding

JOB.42.4-6.text: Job sees the LORD and repents in dust and ashes

JOB.42.10-11.text: The LORD gives Job back his wealth; friends comfort him

JOB.42.12-14.text: The LORD blesses Job with animals and ten children

JOB.42.15-17.text: Job’s daughters receive an inheritance, and Job dies old
